T321 — DEPTH-ENFORCEMENT RULING + OLLAMA->DEEPSEEK FACT-ESTABLISHMENT.

=== ESTABLISHED FACT (real, non-dry-run dispatch) ===

The human's premise on dispatch was that 'Ollama/pi CANNOT call deepseek/pi' and that T320's Ollama->DeepSeek cell was dry-run only (true: --dry-run returns before the subprocess call, so it proved the depth check passed and DEEPSEEK_API_KEY present, not that a child ran). To establish the fact, one REAL dispatch was run from this glm-5.2:cloud console at WEIZIGO_AGENT_DEPTH=unset:

  bin/subagent untracked/T321-probe-capital.md --dspro --wall=300

The probe asked one question with a checkable answer ('What is the capital of France?'), expecting exactly the word 'Paris'. Literal output:

  [runner] argv = pi --provider deepseek --model deepseek-v4-pro -p 'Follow untracked/T321-probe-capital.md
'
  [runner] guards: rss 4096 MB, progress-timeout 600s (10:00), fallback: wall 300s cpu 3600s (silent children), poll = 250 ms
  [runner] process walker: ps (darwin)
  Paris
  [runner] peak RSS by PID: in 4.5 s
  [runner]   pid 43138     194 MB
  [runner] peak total CPU by PID: in 4.5 s
  [runner]   pid 43138        0:00 (0.5s)
  [runner] exit 0 in 4.5 s

The reply was exactly 'Paris'; RC=0; wall 4.5 s. A file target skips the claim wrapper so no kanban row was touched.

CONCLUSION: Ollama -> DeepSeek WORKS end-to-end. The human's stated belief was wrong on this point; the capability is demonstrated. So option (c) (strip DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from Ollama children) is NOT moot — it is the only option that truly closes path 2 — but it changes what existing consoles can do and is held for the human's explicit word. No legitimate Ollama->DeepSeek use is documented (Ollama models run as leaf workers; DeepSeek is dispatched from the human console or a manager via bin/subagent), and the probe found none.

(An earlier one-line marker probe in the same session also ran and wrote a marker file /tmp/weizigo/T321-deepseek-marker.txt = 'PROBE-RAN' and printed 'PROBE-OK', exit 0, 5.8 s; superseded by the canonical capital probe above.)

=== MATRIX CORRECTIONS (per human's direction) ===

1. T320's 'deepseek-v4-pro (d=2) -> DeepSeek REFUSED' cell ran `bin/subagent --dry-run` with NO task argument — it exited 1 for missing arguments, NOT because of the depth cap. The real depth-cap refusal was demonstrated on the glm-5.2(d=2)->DeepSeek cell (proper args, REFUSED, exit 1).

2. Row labels must be by DEPTH (the gate), not by model name. A DeepSeek/pi worker at depth 1 (a manager) CAN dispatch DeepSeek/pi; only a worker at depth >= 2 is refused.

Both corrections are written into docs/infra/agents/subdelegation.md (now 'Reach matrix (T320, corrected T321, 2026-08-03)').

=== RULING: (b) + (a)'s honest documentation; (c) held ===

Option costs (one line each):
  (a) Accept convention — zero code; risk is an accidental recursion burning cloud budget.
  (b) Wrap the Ollama launch — bin/ollama-subagent stamps WEIZIGO_AGENT_DEPTH, increments it, refuses at worker depth; a convention backed by a tool, not a boundary; only helps if used instead of `ollama launch pi`.
  (c) Strip DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from Ollama children — the only real enforcement (closes the demonstrated path 2); breaks any legitimate Ollama->DeepSeek use (none documented, none found).

Implemented: bin/ollama-subagent mirrors bin/subagent's contract for the Ollama path (refuse at WEIZIGO_AGENT_DEPTH >= 2, stamp child at depth 2, run under tools/runner via `ollama launch pi --model <tag> -y -- -p <prompt>`). It does NOT strip DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, so path 2 stays open (only (c) closes it). `ollama launch pi` remains directly callable and unguarded; the three paths are documented as live in subdelegation.md.

Also corrected in subdelegation.md: 'Attribution never asks the model (T321)' — T320 probed the PI_MODEL env var (0/4 correct) which is a DIFFERENT question from 'what model do you believe you are' (2/2 wrong: a deepseek-v4-pro worker said claude-opus-4-5, a glm-5.2 child said GPT-5, neither string on disk beforehand). Rule: attribution reads PI_MODEL or comes from the dispatcher; never from the model's self-report.
